message.reasoning:
Let me evaluate.

C1 Mission concept: Good description of coral reef monitoring mission, users (marine/conservation scientists), rationale, references. But lacks specific mission goals/objectives/requirements detail (no requirements list, no mission objectives quantified). Still, it's clear and referenced. Accomplished range 7-10 or Adequate 4-6? It describes what, users, why needed, with literature. Missing explicit objectives/requirements. I'd say 7 (low Accomplished) or 6. The description is fairly complete with references; I'd give 7.

C2 Project plan: Gantt chart present, task descriptions, information sources? Sources are cited in mission concept but no explicit list of planned information sources beyond references. Plan fits narrative. Contingencies? Not much provision for variations. Adequate-to-Accomplished. I'd say 6-7. Plan is robust-ish but no contingency. Give 6.

C3 Preliminary progress: Completed STK tutorials 1-4, research on Asner's system, mission concept done. Some technical work but no actual results (no orbit calcs, no figures of STK). Note technical error: "geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km" — geostationary is ~35,786 km; 600 km would be LEO. That's a significant technical error. Progress: minor work completed, results description insufficient → Adequate, 4-5. Give 4 or 5. Tutorials completed + research; but no preliminary results. Give 4.

C4 Presentation: Clear structure, headings, well-written, references cited with footnotes matching URLs. Gantt chart clear. Minor issues: footnote-style URLs rather than formal reference list; "geostationary at 600 km" error is technical not presentation. Overall good. Give 7-8. Give 7.

Requirements:
R1: yes — mission concept benefits Australia (GBR), users, rationale.
R2: partial — plan mentions launch/orbit specifics and course material (astrodynamics), but the orbit statement is wrong (geostationary 600 km). Plan relates to space segment though. Met "partial" or "yes"? The plan does relate to space segment applying launch and orbits. But the technical error... requirement is about relating plan to space segment — yes it does. I'd say yes, but note the error in technical_issues. Actually the error undermines; still requirement met. Say yes.
R3: yes — STK selected ("STK Design", "STK Simulations", completed STK tutorials).
R4: yes — Gantt chart.
R5: partial — sources cited in text but no explicit list of planned information sources; references are URLs only. Partial.
R6: partial — tutorials completed, research done, but no preliminary technical results/calculations shown. Partial.

Technical issues: geostationary orbit at 600 km altitude — incorrect; GEO is ~35,786 km; a 600 km orbit cannot be geostationary. Also "Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic" — surface oceans ~30% more acidic since industrial revolution is actually a commonly cited figure (pH dropped 0.1 = 30% increase in acidity), so that's fine. "In 2017, another 50 percent perished" — misinterpretation of the Nat Geo stat (50% of coral in northern/central sections), but minor.

Overall: solid concept and plan, but technical error in orbit and limited preliminary results.
